leverage.exposure: No leveraged position is open and none would be opened by the recommended action. The single bid sits comfortably inside cash with meaningful headroom left over, and the standing rule holds that spending is capped by cash here rather than by the much larger nominal spending power, because a negative balance at the lock scores nothing for the whole matchday. A separate ledger risk did materialise this run and was fixed: the recommendation list hit its display cap and silently stopped rendering the live bid and the current plan, which is exactly the failure mode recorded earlier as dangerous. Five stale rejections were closed to buy back display room, chosen specifically because each is re-derivable from the market data alone without any stored reasoning.

binding_gap: Still the third attacker. With only two attackers the squad has exactly one legal shape, which forces a player with no points history at all into the fielded eleven as a third midfielder. The live bid is precisely the fix: a third attacker unlocks two better shapes, benches the zero-scorer, and is by a wide margin the largest single-move gain available. Nothing else on the board addresses it — the only other attackers listed are a negative scorer at a manager ask, a cameo-level scorer, and a big name the cash cannot reach.

verdict.detail: No action this run. The one timed instruction from the previous briefing has been carried out and confirmed: the Gomis bid was withdrawn and re-placed at the higher figure, and the market now shows Georg as the sole standing offer on that listing. Nothing further to do before the listing resolves this afternoon. The single most important scheduling point: the next run is the LAST one that can act before the listing expires — the run after that fires essentially at the expiry and will be resolving the auction, not bidding in it.

sell.reason: Nothing. Every standing sale candidate stays on hold and the reason is structural rather than a change of view about the players. At eleven there is no legal sale at all. Once the bid lands and the squad is twelve, the funding sales become available again in the previously recorded order, but none is needed — the cash left after the bid is comfortable and there is nothing worth buying with it.

buy.reason: One live bid, already placed, and no second bid under any circumstances. The board added eight listings since the last run and every one is rejected: two fresh Kickbase listings — an Augsburg defender and a Cologne midfielder — plus a wave of six manager relists inside twenty-six minutes. The defender is a sixth defender, which cannot enter the fielded eleven under any shape, and has no points history. The Cologne midfielder has no points history either and his price is a repricing artefact rather than a valuation. The manager wave fails on points-per-euro across the board: the largest premium sits on a player with no points at all, the cheapest premium sits on the worst scorer on the board, and two of the six are same-day markup flips of players their owners bought off the board hours earlier. None is within a factor of five of the live bid on that measure. A second bid is separately impossible: both new Kickbase listings cost more than the cash left after the bid, so bidding on any of them opens a leveraged position, and a negative balance at matchday start scores nothing for the entire matchday.

standing.name: Tidiam Gomis
standing.why: RAISE THE LIVE GOMIS BID FROM 9.400.000 TO 10.400.000. Bj0cr1a stays OPEN (it records the live 9.400.000 bid and must resolve to feed the calibration table); this call records the raise. TWO THINGS CHANGED AT 10:38:34Z AND THEY BOTH POINT THE SAME WAY. (1) SCHELLER WAS LOST. JakobDohr bought 7320 off the Kickbase board at 8.888.888 against mv 6.832.981 = +30,09%, beating Georg's 7.500.000 (+9,76%) by 1.388.888. The rival appeared after TWELVE HOURS of ofc=1 with Georg the sole bidder, which kills the inference B6i4qsx was built on: ofc=1 at any point before expiry is worth NOTHING as evidence of being unopposed, and the "two consecutive sub-mv clearings" reading from the 08:45Z run (Gosens -0,00001%, Mueller -0,07%) was the wrong lesson from a quiet six hours. +30,09% is now the HIGHEST measured clearing premium in the correctly-priced band and it is also the FRESHEST. (2) THE SCHELLER LOSS FREES THE CASH THAT CAPPED THE GOMIS BID. The 9.400.000 figure was set with 7.500.000 simultaneously committed to Scheller, leaving 37.522 of headroom and an explicit instruction not to raise because a raise would open leverage. That constraint is GONE: cash is 16.937.522 and nothing else is committed. WHY 9.400.000 IS NOW A LOSING BID, and this is the mechanism a future run must watch for: the bid was set at 04:45Z against mv 7.014.962 = +34,00%, deliberately ~6 points above the then-high cluster. Gomis's mv has since risen INTRADAY to 7.418.952 (+403.990) despite mvud being 2026-09-02T20:00:00Z - market values in this data move between the nominal daily ticks. The bid did not change but the premium silently eroded to +26,70%, which is now BELOW every datapoint in the high cluster: Scheller +30,09%, ter Horst +27,61%, Ljubicic +27,34%, Vagnoman +27,26%. Georg is sitting under the whole cluster on the best asset on the board. THE NEW NUMBER: 10.400.000 against mv 7.418.952 = +40,18%. That is ~10 percentage points clear of the +30,09% record, and the margin is sized for the erosion risk as well as the rival risk - if mv drifts up another ~400k to ~7,82M by resolution, 10.400.000 is still +33,0%, i.e. still above the record. Benchmarked against the HIGH cluster, never the median: median is now +2,75% and is pure manager-ask noise. DO NOT read the Maluze +308,77% record as licence to bid higher here - that premium was enormous only because Maluze's mv had not caught up with his ap; Gomis's mv already prices him as a 7,4M player. AFFORDABILITY: 10.400.000 against cash 16.937.522 leaves 6.537.522 and opens NO leveraged position, so the negative-balance-scores-zero rule is untouched. This is the ONLY bid to place - do not add a second, see the Onyeka arithmetic in the WATCH. WHY HE IS STILL WORTH IT: ap 176, the largest single fielded gain available. Squad is 11 = 1GK/5DEF/3MID/2ATT with 5-3-2 the ONLY legal shape, which forces Amoako (no points history at all) into the fielded eleven. Gomis is a THIRD ATTACKER: with him the squad is 12 = 1/5/3/3, 5-2-3 becomes legal, Amoako is benched and the fielded total goes 1256 -> 1432 ap. PLUS 176 for one purchase. At 10.400.000 that is 59,1k per point, still the best on the board (Onyeka 60,1k, Castello Jr. 102k, Atubolu 91k, Koenigsdoerffer 302k). FITNESS RE-VERIFIED THIS RUN 2026-09-02T10:5xZ: Ligainsider Verletzte-und-Gesperrte gives Leipzig as Gebel (ACL, 10 months), Baumgartner (3 months) and Ouedraogo (4 weeks) - Gomis is NOT on it. Ligainsider profile /tidiam-gomis_36962/ marks him FIT, 2026/27: 2 appearances, 1 BL start, 1 DFB-Pokal start, 3 assists, 128 minutes. Demichelis 21.08.2026 "Gomis startet gegen Trier". The "angeschlagen raus" note on the profile is dated 08.10.2025 and the RB tweet about the Innenband is 19.08.2025 - both LAST SEASON, date trap unchanged. st=0, stl empty, mvt 1 rising. MD2: Leipzig away at Werder Bremen 2026-09-05T13:30Z, inside the window. MECHANICS: Kickbase has no raise-in-place, so Georg removes the 9.400.000 offer and places 10.400.000 on the same listing. Do this WELL BEFORE the ~16:45Z expiry - Kickbase is pay-your-bid, so bidding early costs nothing and the Scheller rival arrived at the death. Deadline set to 14:00Z to leave slack ahead of the 14:45Z run. UNWIND CEILING: one buy permits exactly one sale, and no sale is needed - see the master plan. RISK STATED HONESTLY: pay-your-bid, so if nobody else bids, 2.981.048 over mv is wasted cash. Accepted - there is nothing else on this board worth buying, and losing ap 176 for a second consecutive run costs far more than cash Georg has no use for before the lock.

movers.reason: No flip clears its cost this run — there are no manager asks below market value, so the mechanism is absent, and the only asks available are all priced above it. Two more rival micro-flips confirm the standing instruction not to copy them: one manager bought and resold a player seventy-six seconds later for a fraction of a percent, and another dumped a negative-scoring defender back to the market at exactly market value for nothing at all. That is motion, not points. Separately, this run found a genuinely new and much larger value mechanic: players enter the game at a floor market value and reprice by more than an order of magnitude within a day. One rival bought a player at that floor this morning. It is recorded as a standing instruction to scan for floor-priced listings every run, with the honest caveat that it is a value play rather than a points play and rests on a single observed repricing so far.
